what: Lamb Weston makes frozen potato products, above all french fries. It buys potatoes from contracted growers, processes them in large plants and ships frozen fries, wedges and hash browns worldwide.
customers: Restaurant chains, above all quick-service burger and chicken chains, plus foodservice distributors, and retailers who sell frozen fries under store brands and under Lamb Weston's own labels.
money: Fries and other frozen potato products for US and Canadian restaurant chains and retailers.
Sales outside North America, including joint-venture plants in Europe and operations in Asia and Latin America.
moat: Potato processing at scale is capital-heavy and the plants must sit near the growing regions, which limits where anyone can build. Lamb Weston has long relationships with the largest burger chains and is one of only a few suppliers able to serve them globally with consistent product.
risks: Restaurant traffic has been weak, and fries are sold by the pound to chains whose own volumes are falling.
The company and its competitors added capacity just as demand softened, so there is more fry capacity than the market needs and pricing has suffered.
Margins are thin: $254.8M of net income on $6.6B of revenue.
Debt is about $4.0B against $68.2M of cash, a heavy load for a food processor with compressed margins.
Potato crop quality and price vary with the weather, and a poor crop raises input costs across a whole season.
opportunities: Fries carry high margins for restaurants, so chains keep promoting them, and long-run global fry consumption has grown steadily.
The shares trade at about 1.1 times sales and 11.9 times EV/EBITDA, a low multiple for a branded food processor.
Cost reduction and plant rationalisation can recover margin without needing volume growth.
Free cash flow is roughly $411.9M, enough to service debt and fund the dividend while capacity spending falls back.
watch: Volume, not price. Lamb Weston can only raise prices so far with its restaurant customers, so the pounds of product shipped each quarter is the clean signal of whether demand is recovering.
